speaker: Other Mother
text: Come along, dear. It's time for your new eyes.

speaker: Other Mother
text: There we are, dear. All finished. Come and meet me upstairs.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Those buttons weren't a gift, dear. They were how I claimed your soul.

speaker: Other Mother
text: You aren't a living child to me any longer. I will feed on what remains of your life.

speaker: Other Mother
text: And now there's nothing left for you to do. I think I'll keep what's left of you.

speaker: Other Mother
text: There. Now everyone has a drink. What a thoughtful host you're becoming.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Hold it steady, sweetheart. Now click each empty glass.

speaker: Other Mother
text: That's our cider jug. We'll top up everyone's glasses after the first course.

speaker: Other Mother
text: The bowl smells of warm honey and summer flowers. What do you think I put in it?

speaker: Other Mother
text: A sharp, fruity scent rises from the bowl, with little purple berry stains at the rim.

speaker: Other Mother
text: The sauce smells of rich cocoa. There are tiny chocolate shavings on the spoon.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Save some room! We'll serve dessert after our little recipe game.

speaker: Other Mother
text: A slice of berry cake for me, please.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Thank you, sweetheart. Don't forget your Other Father.

speaker: Other Mother
text: All tidied away. Stay and chat, or tell us when you're ready to finish.

speaker: Other Mother
text: How is the first bite? Try the other things on your plate, too.

speaker: Other Mother
text: One more taste. Every dish has a little story behind it.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Is there anything else you would like, sweetheart?

speaker: Other Mother
text: You've smelled the sauce. Which ingredient did you recognise?

speaker: Other Mother
text: Inspect the little recipe bowl first. A good cook uses their nose as well as their eyes.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Honey for warmth, berries for sharpness, chocolate for a treat. You'll find a recipe bowl on the table when it's time to guess.

speaker: Other Mother
text: What shall we raise our glasses to?

speaker: Other Mother
text: Perfect? Only because I pay attention to what everyone wants. You do tell me what you want, don't you?

speaker: Other Mother
text: Let's enjoy the evening we have first. There is always something else waiting for us.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Exactly right! A fine nose. Now let's get those desserts served.

speaker: Other Mother
text: You found the secret ingredient. Berry cake for me and cookies for your Other Father, please.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Not quite. Smell the recipe bowl again and look for the clue before trying another ingredient.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Taste as you go, and never stop paying attention. The smallest ingredient can change everything.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Of course. A little help can make a meal feel like something we've made together.

speaker: Other Mother
text: To a lovely evening. Just your plate left to clear, sweetheart.

speaker: Other Mother
text: To taking very good care of one another. I'll drink to that.

speaker: Other Mother
text: To adventures. Though do remember to come back for supper.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Home is where you're wanted, sweetheart. Remember that.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Some doors are closed for their own good. Leave them closed.

speaker: Other Mother
text: There are things here too fragile for curious hands.

speaker: Other Mother
text: You have been watching everything so carefully. So have I.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Perhaps my presents have spoiled you.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Is there something missing from what I have given you?

speaker: Other Mother
text: You needn't concern yourself with every locked door.

speaker: Other Mother
text: A toast to our guest of honour! Come join the neighbours, darling.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Our guest of honour! Take your place by the cake, make a wish, and blow out the candles.

speaker: Other Mother
text: We'll do something else while the delivery route is prepared.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Follow the path, deliver the package, and come back to me, sweetheart.

speaker: Other Mother
text: Getting bored already, sweetheart? Shall I find something else for us to do?

speaker: Other Father
text: That's mine filled. Your Other Mother's glass is still empty.

speaker: Other Father
text: One slice of berry cake. Take that over to your Other Mother's plate.

speaker: Other Father
text: Those cookies are for me! Click my plate to serve them.

speaker: Other Father
text: Could I have the cookies, kiddo?

speaker: Other Father
text: Perfect! You remembered both orders. Now, how about a toast?

speaker: Other Father
text: Thanks, kiddo! Could you top up our cider next? The jug's in the middle.

speaker: Other Father
text: The other dish, please. I've highlighted the one I meant.

speaker: Other Father
text: Three tastes! Which was your favourite? You can tell us at the table. Could you pass me a dish first?

speaker: Other Father
text: What would you like to do?

speaker: Other Father
text: Dinner's better when we have something to talk about, kiddo.

speaker: Other Father
text: I started with a little tune and let it wander. Sometimes the tune seems to know the house better than I do.

speaker: Other Father
text: You pick the rhythm, I'll find the notes. Tap your spoon: slow, quick, quick. There! That's our dinner song.

speaker: Other Father
text: The flowers lean toward anyone who listens. If you visit, look for the little paths between the tallest stems.

speaker: Other Father
text: What shall we raise our glasses to?

speaker: Other Father
text: The roast was lovely, but I always save a little room for cookies. What about you?

speaker: Other Father
text: She likes everything just so. I try to leave a little room for surprises in the music.

speaker: Other Father
text: That's it! A bright little chorus. We ought to remember this one.

speaker: Other Father
text: A quiet tune for a house full of secrets. You have an ear for atmosphere, kiddo.

speaker: Other Father
text: I do what I can. A little patience, a little water, and knowing when to leave things alone.

speaker: Other Father
text: I sometimes wonder that myself. Best not to tell a flower anything you wouldn't sing aloud.

speaker: Other Father
text: That's a toast worth keeping, kiddo. Nobody should have to do everything alone.

speaker: Other Father
text: To all the things we haven't discovered yet!

speaker: Other Father
text: To home. And to finding your own way there.

speaker: Other Father
text: Thank you, kiddo!

speaker: Other Father
text: Music makes a house feel like home, doesn't it? I keep finding new melodies here.

speaker: Other Father
text: The garden has a way of surprising me too. Even the flowers seem to be listening.

speaker: Other Father
text: Fair enough, kiddo. We all need a quiet moment sometimes.

speaker: Other Father
text: Of course. Take your time and enjoy it.

speaker: Other Father
text: Thank you! Right-click the highlighted dish when you're ready to pass it.

speaker: Other Father
text: What have you enjoyed most about the house?

speaker: Other Father
text: Could you give me a hand with the table?

speaker: Other Father
text: So, what have you been getting up to today?

speaker: Other Father
text: Make a wish, kiddo. Ready? Click the cake again and blow!

speaker: Other Father
text: A show souvenir for you: two Perfect Ingots!
